name: com.tedthetaxguy/ted
title: Ted the Tax Guy
description: US tax calculators, IRS deadlines and answers cited to official IRS pages. Not tax advice.

tools.name: estimate_self_employment_tax
tools.description: Compute US federal self-employment tax (Social Security and Medicare, Schedule SE) on a year's net self-employment profit, plus the income tax on that profit and a per-quarter amount. Use it for freelancers, sole proprietors, 1099 contractors and single-member LLC owners. Handles W-2 wages in the same year and the Additional Medicare Tax. Returns exact figures from Ted's tax calculator, the official IRS sources behind them, and the tax year used. Federal only; no state tax.

net_profit.description: Net self-employment profit for the year (Schedule C net profit, after business expenses), in US dollars (whole dollars, no symbols)

tax_year.description: The tax year the figures are for (2025, 2026, 2027). Leave it out for the default: last year's return until April 15, then the current year.

filing_status.description: Filing status: single, mfj (married filing jointly), mfs (married filing separately) or hoh (head of household). Default single.

w2_wages.description: W-2 wages from a job in the same year, if any (they use up the Social Security wage cap first), in US dollars (whole dollars, no symbols)

tools.name: quarterly_estimate
tools.description: Compute US federal quarterly estimated tax payments (Form 1040-ES) for self-employed people and people with side income. Four modes: catch_up (behind on this year's payments: what is owed and what to pay by the next due date), set_aside (W-2 job plus side business: share of side profit to set aside), safe_harbor (the prior-year 100% or 110% safe harbor that avoids the underpayment penalty), required (the required annual payment and per-quarter amount). Returns figures, due dates, official sources and the tax year used.

mode.description: catch_up: self-employed and behind on this year's estimated payments (needs profit, optional paid_so_far). set_aside: a W-2 job plus a side business, what share of side profit to set aside (needs profit and w2_wages). safe_harbor: the prior-year safe harbor that avoids the underpayment penalty (needs prior_year_tax and prior_year_agi, optional withholding and side_profit). required: the Form 1040-ES required annual payment and per-quarter amount (needs profit, optional w2_wages, withholding, prior_year_tax, prior_year_agi).

tax_year.description: The tax year the figures are for (2025, 2026, 2027). Leave it out for the default: last year's return until April 15, then the current year.

filing_status.description: Filing status: single, mfj (married filing jointly), mfs (married filing separately) or hoh (head of household). Default single.

profit.description: Expected self-employment profit for the year, in US dollars (whole dollars, no symbols)

w2_wages.description: W-2 wages from a job for the year, in US dollars (whole dollars, no symbols)

paid_so_far.description: catch_up: estimated payments already made for the year, in US dollars (whole dollars, no symbols)

prior_year_tax.description: Last year's total tax (Form 1040 total tax line), in US dollars (whole dollars, no symbols)

prior_year_agi.description: Last year's adjusted gross income, in US dollars (whole dollars, no symbols)

withholding.description: This year's federal income tax withholding from a job, in US dollars (whole dollars, no symbols)

side_profit.description: safe_harbor: this year's side-business profit, in US dollars (whole dollars, no symbols)

tools.name: tax_deadline
tools.description: List upcoming US federal tax deadlines for a filer type (individual, self_employed, s_corp, partnership, employer) from a date in 2026 or 2027, or check what is due on a given date. Covers Form 1040 and extensions, quarterly estimated payments, S-corp and partnership returns, Form 2553, W-2, 1099-NEC, 940 and 941. Dates already moved for weekends and legal holidays, each with its official source. Calendar-year filers; no state deadlines.

filer_type.description: Whose deadlines: individual (Form 1040 filers), self_employed (freelancers, sole proprietors, single-member LLCs), s_corp, partnership (multi-member LLCs), employer (payroll forms), or all. Default all.

date.description: List deadlines on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD (2026 or 2027). Default today, US Eastern time. To check one date, pass it and read whether the first row falls on it.

count.description: How many deadlines to return, 1 to 20. Default 5.

tools.name: tips_overtime_deduction
tools.description: Compute the 2025 law's federal deduction for qualified tips or qualified overtime pay (2025 to 2028): the deduction after the yearly cap and the income phase-out, eligibility (for example married filing separately does not qualify) and the federal income tax it saves. For overtime, give the overtime premium, or hours and the regular rate. Returns figures, official sources and the tax year used.

kind.description: tips: the qualified tips deduction. overtime: the qualified overtime compensation deduction (the half-time premium only).

magi.description: Modified adjusted gross income for the year (for most people, AGI), in US dollars (whole dollars, no symbols)

tax_year.description: The tax year the figures are for (2025, 2026, 2027). Leave it out for the default: last year's return until April 15, then the current year.

filing_status.description: Filing status: single, mfj (married filing jointly), mfs (married filing separately) or hoh (head of household). Default single.

amount.description: tips: qualified tips received for the year. overtime: the overtime premium (the extra half of time-and-a-half), if known, in US dollars (whole dollars, no symbols)

overtime_hours.description: overtime only, instead of amount: hours paid at time-and-a-half in the year

regular_rate.description: overtime only, with overtime_hours: the regular hourly rate in dollars

tools.name: ask_ted
tools.description: Ask Ted the Tax Guy, an AI tax guide, one US federal or state tax question in plain words. Ted searches only indexed official IRS (and some state tax agency) pages and answers in a few short paragraphs with numbered citations [n] that map to the returned source links. It declines topics outside US tax and says so when no official page answers. Slower than the calculators (often 10 to 40 seconds) and rate limited: for a figure from the user's own numbers, prefer the calculator tools. General information, not tax advice.

question.description: One US tax question in plain words, with any numbers that matter, e.g. 'Can I deduct my home office if I rent?'

tax_year.description: The tax year the figures are for (2025, 2026, 2027). Leave it out for the default: last year's return until April 15, then the current year.
